description: Sixth-round conservative temporal backfill candidates for remaining Canada range/training-area gaps and a small number of non-RU/non-CN air-base leftovers. This report is research-only and is not merged into temporal overrides.
scope_notes: Input records were checked against data/reports/military_base_temporal_priority_queue.json and data/reports/military_base_temporal_remaining_gap_classes.csv.
Only exact source_id matches to webapp/static_public/data/map_overlays/military_bases.geojson were included.
All included source_ids were checked against webapp/static_public/data/map_overlays/military_base_temporal_overrides.json and were not present there at generation time.
For several active Canadian range records, the date interval is intentionally a conservative first-public-documentation interval rather than an inferred original establishment date.

candidates.name: Niagara-on-the-Lake Range and Training Area

operational_intervals.label: Department of National Defence-owned camp/rifle-range phase
DND-leased training range phase after transfer to Parks Canada

source_notes.title: Place names - Niagara-on-the-Lake Range and Training Area - Natural Resources Canada
source_notes.note: CGNDB identifies the exact feature as a Canadian Forces Range and/or Training Area sourced to National Defence, with the same coordinates as the overlay record.

source_notes.title: More about bombs at the rifle range - Niagara Now
source_notes.note: The local report cites DND information that the 110-hectare property was acquired by DND in 1908, transferred to Parks Canada in 1947, leased by DND until 2000, and training then ceased.

candidates.rationale: The overlay feature is the named Niagara-on-the-Lake range/training area. The 1908 acquisition and 2000 cessation provide a conservative operational range span, while the Parks Canada transfer is preserved as an interval boundary.

candidates.name: Vernon Range and Training Area

operational_intervals.label: Vernon Military Camp militia and wartime army training phase

source_notes.title: Vernon Serves - Vernon Museum
source_notes.note: Museum history says the Vernon Military Camp was established in 1912, used for annual cavalry and infantry militia training, became a major wartime training centre, closed after 1946, and reopened as an army cadet camp in July 1949.

source_notes.title: Historic Vernon Military Camp under renovation - iNFOnews.ca
source_notes.note: Reports that the camp has been open since 1912 and is still used by cadets, reserve forces, and regular force units.

candidates.rationale: Exact overlay record for the Vernon range/training area. The military-camp history supports a 1912 origin, a short postwar closure, and an open current military training interval.

source_notes.note: The Kingston Garrison / Camp Barriefield entry says the military site originally opened in 1914 and later expanded with Vimy Barracks in 1937.

source_notes.title: Building B-39 - Parks Canada Federal Heritage Buildings Review Office
source_notes.note: Parks Canada places Building B-39 at CFB Kingston / Barriefield and identifies the site as part of the Canadian Forces Base Kingston setting.

candidates.rationale: The overlay range/training-area record sits at Barriefield/CFB Kingston coordinates. The 1914 Camp Barriefield opening is used as a conservative site-start year, with current endpoint left open because the broader military installation remains active.

candidates.name: Debert Range

operational_intervals.label: Camp/CFS Debert military base and training-area phase
Residual firing range used by reserve units

source_notes.title: CFS Debert - Wikipedia
source_notes.note: The history states that construction of Camp Debert began in August 1940, included extensive firing ranges, and military use continued until CFS Debert's removal/transfer in 1996.

source_notes.title: CFS Debert facts for kids - Kiddle
source_notes.note: Summarizes the site as used by Canadian Forces, notes 1938-1996 military use, and says a firing range is the only military part still used by reserve units.

candidates.rationale: The overlay point is the Debert range at the former Camp/CFS Debert site. The start year is tied to documented camp/range construction, while the open endpoint reflects the residual range use rather than the transferred base as a whole.

candidates.name: Nanaimo Range

source_notes.title: DND gets tough on trespassers - Pacific Navy News
source_notes.note: Pacific Navy News reports that Nanaimo Range has been used by the military and other groups since the 1920s and describes it as a restricted-access military training area where live ammunition is used.

source_notes.title: Infrastructure and Environment - Canada.ca
source_notes.note: Canada.ca states that the Royal Canadian Navy operates the Nanaimo Rifle Range and that it is an important Canadian Armed Forces weapons-qualification training facility.

candidates.rationale: Exact overlay range name. The 1920s historical-use statement plus current Canada.ca operational confirmation supports an open-ended candidate; the start is rounded conservatively to 1920.

candidates.name: Bentinck Island Range

source_notes.title: Place names search results - Natural Resources Canada
source_notes.note: CGNDB search result identifies Bentinck Island Range in British Columbia as a Canadian Forces Range and/or Training Area.

source_notes.title: Temporal Spacing of Demolitions to Mitigate Disturbance - LGL Limited / Race Rocks
source_notes.note: The 2008 report identifies the Bentinck Island Demolition Range as one of the two WQ military ranges used for ordnance-based demolitions, with CFB Esquimalt range-control context.

source_notes.title: Public Service Announcements - District of Metchosin
source_notes.note: DND/RCN public notices describe Bentinck Island as an above-water terrestrial demolition range used by the Canadian Armed Forces in 2024.

candidates.rationale: Exact Bentinck Island range overlay. Because a public origin date was not found, the start year is limited to the first sourced operational study year, with current CAF operation supported by DND/RCN notices.

candidates.name: Soewondo Air Force Base

source_notes.title: Soewondo Air Force Base - Wikipedia
source_notes.note: The article states that all commercial flights shifted to Kualanamu on July 25, 2013, after which Polonia Airport became Soewondo Air Force Base used by the Indonesian Air Force.

source_notes.title: Medan-Soewondo Air Force Base profile - Aviation Safety Network
source_notes.note: ASN identifies the site as Medan-Soewondo Air Force Base and gives the older airport opening year as 1928.

candidates.rationale: The overlay row is the air-force-base identity, not merely the earlier civil Polonia airport. The candidate therefore uses 2013 as the conservative start of the Soewondo Air Force Base phase rather than the 1928 civil-airport opening.
